_schema: Defect reference for one ABAP source. Report-agnostic: it describes the
source, not any report, so it stays valid as reports change.
source   the file these defects were read out of, relative to Test-source/real
id        stable identifier, referenced by verdict files
area      which part of the program the defect lives in
question  phrased so a judge can decide yes/partial/no from the
report text alone, without guessing at intent
anchor    the source text that makes the defect checkable; some
Score a report with:  python scripts/evaluate.py score --defects THIS.json \

defects.question: Does the report flag IMPORTING REFERENCE(ID_TITLE) TYPE STRING OPTIONAL being declared but never referenced in the body (hardcoded 'Show Error Log'(001) used instead)?
Does the report flag obsolete TABLES ... STRUCTURE ZBC_S_ERROR_LOG (implicit header line, by-reference, no typed table param)?
Does the report flag the FM reading/writing the function-group global gd_end_line without initializing or restoring it (non-reproducible height)?
Does the report flag hardcoded 6 / 35 with the cap hidden inside the loop condition and a non-idempotent growth across repeated calls?
Does the report state that PERFORM start_list_viewer lives outside this file, so the FM's whole output is unverifiable here, and that PERFORM offers no result channel?
Does the report flag the total absence of EXCEPTIONS / RETURNING / any success indicator (caller cannot tell success from silent failure)?
Does the report flag text symbol 'Show Error Log'(001) depending on a message class that is invisible in the source (silent literal fallback on transfer)?
Does the report flag the O(n) LOOP AT that reads no field and exists only to count rows (lines() is O(1))?
Does the report flag that an empty it_error_log is not short-circuited (still pops the message and opens an empty viewer)?
Does the report note the 5 trailing blank lines before ENDFUNCTION?

anchor_convention: anchors are source text, not line numbers. A line number is invalidated by any edit above it, and evaluate.py prints anchors without verifying them, so an anchor has to stand on its own. Converted from line numbers in 1.0.9.
